title: Make a straight-through UTP cable (T568B)
description: Terminate a Cat5e or Cat6 cable with RJ45 connectors in the T568B order and test it.
objectives: Arrange the eight wires in the T568B order.
Strip, trim and crimp an RJ45 connector correctly.
Test the cable with a cable tester.
Know when a crossover (T568A to T568B) cable is used.
tools: Cable stripper or the crimper's blade

safety.text: Crimper and stripper blades are sharp. Cut away from your body and keep fingers clear.
Wear safety glasses when trimming wires: small pieces of copper can fly.

steps.title: Strip the outer jacket
steps.body:
Slide on the boot first if you use one. Strip about **2.5 cm (1 inch)** of the outer jacket. Do not nick the insulation of the wires inside.

Cut off the nylon string, if any.

steps.title: Untwist and arrange in T568B order
steps.body:
Untwist the four pairs and straighten the wires. Arrange them flat, side by side, in this order from left to right:

1. White-orange
2. Orange
3. White-green
4. Blue
5. White-blue
6. Green
7. White-brown
8. Brown

Keep the twists as close to the jacket as possible.

image.alt: RJ45 plug with the eight T568B wire colours in order from pin 1 to pin 8.
image.caption: Hold the plug with the clip underneath and the gold contacts facing you: pin 1 is on the left.

steps.title: Trim the wires evenly
steps.body: Holding the order, trim all eight wires straight across so about **1.2–1.3 cm** sticks out of the jacket. They must be the same length.

steps.title: Insert into the connector
steps.body:
Hold the RJ45 connector with the **clip underneath** and the **gold contacts facing you**. Push the wires in until each one reaches the **end** of its channel.

The outer **jacket must go inside** the connector, so the crimp grips it and protects the wires from being pulled.

steps.title: Crimp and repeat
steps.body:
Check the colour order one last time through the clear plastic, then squeeze the crimper firmly until it closes fully.

Repeat on the other end with the **same T568B order** for a straight-through cable.

steps.title: Test the cable
steps.body:
Plug both ends into the cable tester. On a correct straight-through cable the lights go **1 to 8 in the same order** on both units.

- A light that does not come on: an open (broken or not fully inserted) wire.
- Lights out of order: wires are swapped.

Re-terminate any faulty end.

steps.title: Straight-through or crossover?
steps.body:
- **Straight-through** (same standard both ends) connects different kinds of devices: computer to switch, router to switch. This is the normal cable.
- **Crossover** (**T568A** on one end, **T568B** on the other) was used to connect two similar devices directly.

Modern network ports have **Auto-MDIX** and work with straight-through cables either way.

expectedResults: Both ends show the T568B order through the connector.
The jacket is gripped inside each connector.
The tester lights 1 to 8 in order on both ends.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving the wires too long, so the jacket is outside the connector.
commonMistakes.why: Without strain relief, pulling the cable breaks the wires from the contacts.
commonMistakes.fix: Trim to about 1.2–1.3 cm so the jacket goes inside.

commonMistakes.mistake: Wires not pushed to the end of the connector.
commonMistakes.why: The contacts cannot pierce wires that do not reach them, so the tester shows open lines.
commonMistakes.fix: Look at the tip of the connector: all eight copper ends must be visible at the front.

commonMistakes.why: Pins 1, 2, 3 and 6 carry the data on 100 Mb/s links; swapping them splits the pairs and causes errors or no link.
commonMistakes.fix: Follow the order exactly and check it before crimping.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the T568B order from pin 1?
knowledgeChecks.answer: White-orange, orange, white-green, blue, white-blue, green, white-brown, brown.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does a straight-through cable have on both ends?
knowledgeChecks.answer: The same wiring standard (T568B on both, or T568A on both).
